1. What Are We Forecasting?

The Target Outcome Variable

  • Target Variable (\(y_t\)): Daily Estimated Avoidable Deaths (EAD) \[\text{EAD}_t = \sum_{i \in \text{Admissions}_t} \Big[ p_i(\text{delay}_i, \mathbf{z}_i) - p_i(0, \mathbf{z}_i) \Big]\]
    • \(\mathbf{z}_i\): Baseline patient case-mix vector (age, triage acuity, comorbidities).
    • \(\text{delay}_i\): Hours delayed in Emergency Department (ED) awaiting an inpatient hospital bed.
    • \(p_i(\cdot)\): 30-day mortality risk model.
  • Forecasting Objective: Generate daily forecasts over a 10-day horizon (\(h = 1, \dots, 10\) days ahead) using near-real-time operational and patient-flow data.
  • Evaluation Criteria: Days 1–5 (\(\text{MSE}_{1\text{–}5\text{d}}\)) and Days 6–10 (\(\text{MSE}_{6\text{–}10\text{d}}\)).

Key Forecasting Constraints & Rules

  • Midday Forecasting Cut-off: Forecasts for days \(D+1\) to \(D+10\) can only use information available up to midday on day \(D\).
  • Strict 3-Day Reporting Lag:
    Because of clinical validation and mortality verification lags, the true target variable \(y\) is only known up to \(D-3\).
    • On Day \(D\), the most recent verified observation available is \(y_{D-3}\).
  • Sliding Evaluation Windows: 131 sliding 10-day forecast windows evaluated across the hold-out test period (October 2025 – March 2026).

2. Model: Markov-Switching AutoRegressive Regression (MS-ARR)

MS-ARR Formulation

\[ y_t \mid (r_t = r) = \beta_{0}^{(r)} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{t-i} + \sum_{m=p+1}^{M} \beta_{m}^{(r)} X_{tm} + \epsilon_t \]

where \(\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(0, \sigma_r^2\right)\) is \(i.i.d.\) Gaussian noise with regime-specific variance \(\sigma_r^2\).

  • To model regime dynamics, we assume that the latent process \(\{r_t\}\) satisfies the first-order Markov property:

\[ P(r_t = j \mid r_{1:t-1}) = P(r_t = j \mid r_{t-1}), \qquad j \in \mathcal{R}, \; t \ge 2. \]

  • The transition probabilities between states form the transition matrix \(\mathbf{P}\):

\[ \mathbf{P} = \begin{pmatrix} p_{11} & \cdots & p_{1K} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ p_{K1} & \cdots & p_{KK} \end{pmatrix}. \]

Notation & Definitions

  • \(y_t\): Observed number of avoidable deaths at time \(t\)
  • \(r_t\): Unobserved (latent) operational regime at time \(t\)
  • \(X_{tm}\): Exogenous predictors (cyclical, calendar, operational indicators)
  • \(\beta_{0}^{(r)}\): Regime-specific baseline intercept
  • \(\beta_{i}^{(r)}\): Autoregressive coefficients associated with the \(i\)-th lag in regime \(r\)
  • \(\beta_{m}^{(r)}\): Coefficients for exogenous covariates in regime \(r\)
  • \(K\): Total number of regimes (\(\mathcal{R} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}\), here \(K = 2\))

Parameter Estimation & Forecasting Theory

Parameter Estimation of MS-ARR

Model parameters are estimated using the Expectation–Maximization (EM) algorithm (Baum–Welch algorithm), which iteratively refines the full parameter vector:

\[ \theta = \{\beta^{(r)}, \sigma_r^2, \mathbf{P}, \boldsymbol{\pi} \}_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \]

by maximising the marginal log-likelihood of the observed EAD time series \(y_{1:T} = (y_1, \ldots, y_T)\).

NoteEM Algorithm (The Forward-Backward Algorithm - Baum-Welch)

Let \(k\) denote the iteration index. The algorithm iterates between:

\[ \begin{aligned} &\textbf{E-step:} \quad Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)}) = \mathbb{E}_{\,r_{1:T} \mid y_{1:T},\, \theta^{(k)}} \left[ \log p(y_{1:T}, r_{1:T} \mid \theta) \right] \\[8pt] &\textbf{M-step:} \quad \theta^{(k+1)} = \arg\max_{\theta}\, Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)}) \\[8pt] &\textbf{Convergence:} \quad \theta^{(0)} \;\rightarrow\; \text{E-step} \;\rightarrow\; \text{M-step} \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(1)} \;\rightarrow\; \cdots \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(k+1)} \end{aligned} \]

Forecasting with MS-ARR

Let \(P(r_T = i \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T})\) denote the filtered posterior probability of being in regime \(i\) at time \(T\). The \(h\)-step-ahead regime probabilities evolve according to:

\[ P(r_{T+h} = j \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T}) = \sum_{i=1}^{K} P(r_{T+h-1} = i \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T}) \, p_{ij}, \qquad h \ge 1. \]

Conditional on regime \(r_{T+h} = r\), the \(h\)-step-ahead forecast is generated from the regime-specific autoregressive equation:

\[ \hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)} = \beta_{0}^{(r)} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{T+h-i} + \sum_{m=1}^{M} \beta_{p+m}^{(r)} \, X_{T+h,m} \]

The final point forecast at horizon \(h\) is computed as a probability-weighted mixture over all regimes:

\[ \hat{y}_{T+h} = \sum_{r=1}^{K} P(r_{T+h} = r \mid y_{1:T}) \, \hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)}. \]

4. Data Preparation & Python Forecasting Pipeline

Feature Engineering & Input Data

The target time series (ead) is accompanied by calendar, cyclical Fourier annual seasonality features, and rolling quantiles designed to capture baseline capacity saturation.

Python End-to-End Forecasting Pipeline

Below is the concise, production-ready modeling workflow leveraging peshbeen and scikit-learn:

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
from peshbeen.transformations import rolling_quantile                            
from peshbeen.models import ms_arr

# 1. Load data with date index
ead_dff = pd.read_csv("ead_data.csv", index_col="date")
H = 5
target_var = "ead"
cat_vars = ["day", "month", "holiday"]

# 2. Partition historical training set and future exogenous covariates
train_ead = ead_dff[:-H]
future_exog = ead_dff[-H:].drop(columns=target_var)

# 3. Categorical encoding & lag transformations
ohe_encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False, handle_unknown='ignore', drop='first')
transformation_function = [
    rolling_quantile(window_size=49, quantile=0.2, shift=10, min_samples=49)
]

# 4. Initialize and fit MS-ARR model
ms_mod = ms_arr(
    n_components=2, 
    lags=[4, 8, 10],
    target_col=target_var,
    cat_variables=cat_vars,
    categorical_encoder=ohe_encoder,
    n_iter=100,
    lag_transform=transformation_function,
    random_state=42
)
ms_mod.fit(train_ead)

# 5. Generate H-step-ahead forecasts
forecasts = ms_mod.forecast(H=H, exog=future_exog)

5. Point Forecast Evaluation: 120-Day Out-of-Sample Horizon

Below, MS-ARR point forecasts are evaluated across a 120-day rolling out-of-sample evaluation window (24 updates \(\times\) 5-day step forecasts) compared directly against actual verified patient harm.

[!NOTE] Forecasts are recursively generated every 5 days, yielding 24 evaluation cycles across the 120-day horizon.

6. Beyond Point Forecasting: Uncertainty Quantification & Peak Signals

While point forecasts capture the conditional mean, operational decision-makers in emergency care require probabilistic fan charts, distribution tails, and calibrated surge triggers.

Can Point Forecasts Capture Peak Dynamics?

The interactive plot below demonstrates 10,000 simulated forecast trajectories. Use the built-in slider to inspect scenario density and compare the conditional point forecast against extreme surge realizations:

Predictive Distribution Across Horizons (\(h = 1 \dots 5\))

Ridgeline kernel density estimates (KDE) demonstrate how uncertainty widens across horizons, showing where the actual outcome landed relative to the conditional point forecast and the 95th percentile risk threshold:

Can Calibrated Uncertainty Bounds Capture Peaks in EAD?

By constructing 80% and 90% predictive intervals, we can assess empirical coverage reliability over the 120-day holdout:

Operationalizing Forecasts into Actionable Peak Signals

In healthcare operations, a point forecast often under-predicts the magnitude of extreme surges. By coupling the upper quantile ceiling with an operational escalation threshold (\(\text{th}\)), clinical teams can preemptively activate surge protocols:

## 2. Model: Markov-Switching AutoRegressive Regression (MS-ARR)

:::: {.columns style="display: flex; gap: 30px; margin-top: 1.5em;"}

::: {.column style="width: 62%; border-right: 2px solid #D2DFDF; padding-right: 28px;"}

### MS-ARR Formulation

$$
y_t \mid (r_t = r) = \beta_{0}^{(r)} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{t-i} + \sum_{m=p+1}^{M} \beta_{m}^{(r)} X_{tm} + \epsilon_t
$$

[where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(0, \sigma_r^2\right)$ is $i.i.d.$ Gaussian noise with regime-specific variance $\sigma_r^2$.]{style="display: block; padding-left: 1.2em; color: #475569; margin-bottom: 1em;"}

- To model regime dynamics, we assume that the latent process $\{r_t\}$ satisfies the first-order Markov property:

$$
P(r_t = j \mid r_{1:t-1}) = P(r_t = j \mid r_{t-1}), \qquad j \in \mathcal{R}, \; t \ge 2.
$$

- The transition probabilities between states form the transition matrix $\mathbf{P}$:

$$
\mathbf{P} =
\begin{pmatrix}
p_{11} & \cdots & p_{1K} \\
\vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
p_{K1} & \cdots & p_{KK}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

:::

::: {.column style="width: 38%; padding-left: 20px; font-size: 0.95em; line-height: 1.55;"}

### Notation & Definitions

- $y_t$: Observed number of avoidable deaths at time $t$
- $r_t$: Unobserved (latent) operational regime at time $t$
- $X_{tm}$: Exogenous predictors (cyclical, calendar, operational indicators)
- $\beta_{0}^{(r)}$: Regime-specific baseline intercept
- $\beta_{i}^{(r)}$: Autoregressive coefficients associated with the $i$-th lag in regime $r$
- $\beta_{m}^{(r)}$: Coefficients for exogenous covariates in regime $r$
- $K$: Total number of regimes ($\mathcal{R} = \{1, 2, \ldots, K\}$, here $K = 2$)

:::

::::

### Parameter Estimation & Forecasting Theory

:::: {.columns style="display: flex; gap: 28px; margin-top: 1.5em;"}

::: {.column width="50%"}

#### Parameter Estimation of MS-ARR

Model parameters are estimated using the **Expectation–Maximization (EM)** algorithm (Baum–Welch algorithm), which iteratively refines the full parameter vector:

$$
\theta = \{\beta^{(r)}, \sigma_r^2, \mathbf{P}, \boldsymbol{\pi} \}_{r \in \mathcal{R}}
$$

by maximising the marginal log-likelihood of the observed EAD time series $y_{1:T} = (y_1, \ldots, y_T)$.

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
##### EM Algorithm (The Forward-Backward Algorithm - Baum-Welch)

Let $k$ denote the iteration index. The algorithm iterates between:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{E-step:} \quad 
Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)}) 
=
\mathbb{E}_{\,r_{1:T} \mid y_{1:T},\, \theta^{(k)}} 
\left[
\log p(y_{1:T}, r_{1:T} \mid \theta)
\right]
\\[8pt]
&\textbf{M-step:} \quad 
\theta^{(k+1)} 
=
\arg\max_{\theta}\,
Q(\theta \mid \theta^{(k)})
\\[8pt]
&\textbf{Convergence:} \quad 
\theta^{(0)} \;\rightarrow\; \text{E-step} \;\rightarrow\; \text{M-step} \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(1)} \;\rightarrow\; \cdots \;\rightarrow\; \theta^{(k+1)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

#### Forecasting with MS-ARR

Let $P(r_T = i \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T})$ denote the filtered posterior probability of being in regime $i$ at time $T$. The $h$-step-ahead regime probabilities evolve according to:

$$
P(r_{T+h} = j \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T})
=
\sum_{i=1}^{K}
P(r_{T+h-1} = i \mid \mathcal{O}_{1:T}) \, p_{ij},
\qquad h \ge 1.
$$

Conditional on regime $r_{T+h} = r$, the $h$-step-ahead forecast is generated from the regime-specific autoregressive equation:

$$
\hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)}
=
\beta_{0}^{(r)}
+
\sum_{i=1}^{p}
\beta_{i}^{(r)} \, y_{T+h-i}
+
\sum_{m=1}^{M}
\beta_{p+m}^{(r)} \, X_{T+h,m}
$$

The final point forecast at horizon $h$ is computed as a probability-weighted mixture over all regimes:

$$
\hat{y}_{T+h}
=
\sum_{r=1}^{K}
P(r_{T+h} = r \mid y_{1:T}) \, \hat{y}_{T+h}^{(r)}.
$$

:::

### Regime Switches in EAD History

Below, the historical EAD trajectory is displayed alongside the filtered posterior probability of occupying **Regime 2 (Peak Risk)**. Notice how sudden shifts in avoidable mortality correspond to heightened peak-risk probabilities.

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_hmm_df = model_res['hmm_df']
_last180 = _hmm_df.iloc[-180:].copy()
_dates = _last180.index
_target = _last180['ead'].values
_prob_surge = _last180['regime_2'].values

# Colormap from teal (0 = Normal) to amber (0.5) to coral/crimson (1 = Surge)
_cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list('regime_cmap', ['#20808D', '#D97706', '#C93B2B'])

_fig, (_ax1, _ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(18, 8.5), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [1.15, 1]})
_fig.patch.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')
_ax1.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')
_ax2.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')

# Subplot 1: Time Series colored by continuous probability
_norm_dates = np.arange(len(_dates))
_ax1.fill_between(_norm_dates, 0, _target, color='#20808D', alpha=0.06)

_points = np.array([_norm_dates, _target]).T.reshape(-1, 1, 2)
_segments = np.concatenate([_points[:-1], _points[1:]], axis=1)

_lc = LineCollection(_segments, cmap=_cmap, linewidth=3.2, zorder=5)
_lc.set_array(_prob_surge)
_ax1.add_collection(_lc)
_ax1.set_xlim(0, len(_dates)-1)
_ax1.set_ylim(0, max(_target) * 1.15)
_ax1.scatter(_norm_dates, _target, c=_prob_surge, cmap=_cmap, s=40, zorder=6, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8)

_ax1.set_ylabel('Avoidable Deaths', fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C')
_ax1.set_title('Estimated Avoidable Deaths (180 Days) with Regime Changes (Teal = Normal, Red = Peak Risk)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C', pad=12)
_ax1.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.35, color='#cbd5e1')
_ax1.tick_params(labelsize=12)

# Subplot 2: Continuous Posterior Probability P(Surge)
_ax2.plot(_norm_dates, _prob_surge, color='#C93B2B', linewidth=2.8, zorder=5, label='Filtered Probability P(Peak Risk | Past Observations)')
_ax2.fill_between(_norm_dates, 0, _prob_surge, color='#C93B2B', alpha=0.25, zorder=2)
_ax2.fill_between(_norm_dates, _prob_surge, 1, color='#20808D', alpha=0.08, zorder=2)
```

## 4. Data Preparation & Python Forecasting Pipeline

### Feature Engineering & Input Data

The target time series (`ead`) is accompanied by calendar, cyclical Fourier annual seasonality features, and rolling quantiles designed to capture baseline capacity saturation.

```{python .marimo}
# Interactive table view of operational input dataset
_df_display = ead_dff_raw.copy()
_df_display.rename(columns={'sin_1_365.25': 'sin_365 (Annual)'}, inplace=True)
for _c in _df_display.columns:
    if _df_display[_c].dtype == 'float64':
        _df_display[_c] = _df_display[_c].round(4 if _c == 'sin_365 (Annual)' else 2)

mo.ui.table(_df_display, page_size=8, selection=None)
```

### Python End-to-End Forecasting Pipeline

Below is the concise, production-ready modeling workflow leveraging `peshbeen` and `scikit-learn`:

```python
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
from peshbeen.transformations import rolling_quantile                            
from peshbeen.models import ms_arr

# 1. Load data with date index
ead_dff = pd.read_csv("ead_data.csv", index_col="date")
H = 5
target_var = "ead"
cat_vars = ["day", "month", "holiday"]

# 2. Partition historical training set and future exogenous covariates
train_ead = ead_dff[:-H]
future_exog = ead_dff[-H:].drop(columns=target_var)

# 3. Categorical encoding & lag transformations
ohe_encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False, handle_unknown='ignore', drop='first')
transformation_function = [
    rolling_quantile(window_size=49, quantile=0.2, shift=10, min_samples=49)
]

# 4. Initialize and fit MS-ARR model
ms_mod = ms_arr(
    n_components=2, 
    lags=[4, 8, 10],
    target_col=target_var,
    cat_variables=cat_vars,
    categorical_encoder=ohe_encoder,
    n_iter=100,
    lag_transform=transformation_function,
    random_state=42
)
ms_mod.fit(train_ead)

# 5. Generate H-step-ahead forecasts
forecasts = ms_mod.forecast(H=H, exog=future_exog)
```

### Preprocessed Model Feature Matrix

The full matrix fed into the EM optimizer incorporates autoregressive lags, one-hot encoded days and months, and rolling shifted saturation signals:

```{python .marimo}
# Interactive table of preprocessed feature data

_full_dff.rename(columns={'sin_1_365.25': 'sin_365 (Annual)'}, inplace=True)
for _c in _full_dff.columns:
    if _full_dff[_c].dtype == 'float64':
        _full_dff[_c] = _full_dff[_c].round(4 if _c == 'sin_365 (Annual)' else 2)

mo.ui.table(_full_dff, page_size=8, selection=None)
```

## 5. Point Forecast Evaluation: 120-Day Out-of-Sample Horizon

Below, MS-ARR point forecasts are evaluated across a **120-day rolling out-of-sample evaluation window** (24 updates $\times$ 5-day step forecasts) compared directly against actual verified patient harm.

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_train_last90 = cv_data['training_last90']
_cv_df = cv_data['cv_results']
_origin_date = _train_last90.index[-1]

_fig_cv, _ax_cv = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 7.5), facecolor='#FBFAF4')
_ax_cv.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')

# Historical Training Data (Last 90 Days)
_ax_cv.plot(_train_last90.index, _train_last90['ead'], color='#64748b', linewidth=2.2, label='Historical Training EAD (Last 90 Days)', zorder=3)
_ax_cv.fill_between(_train_last90.index, 0, _train_last90['ead'], color='#64748b', alpha=0.06, zorder=2)

# Major separator between training and CV evaluation
_ax_cv.axvline(_origin_date, color='#0B363C', linestyle='--', linewidth=2.4, zorder=8, label=f'Forecast Origin ({_origin_date.strftime("%b %d, %Y")})')

# Out-of-Sample Actuals
_conn_dates = [_origin_date] + list(_cv_df['fold_index'])

_ax_cv.plot(_conn_dates, _conn_actuals, color='#0B363C', linewidth=2.8, marker='o', markersize=4.2, label='Actual Observed EAD (Out-of-Sample)', zorder=6)

_ax_cv.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, facecolor='#ffffff', edgecolor='#cbd5e1', fontsize=12, ncol=1)

                 fontsize=17, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C', pad=18)

_ax_cv.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.35, color='#cbd5e1')
_ax_cv.tick_params(labelsize=12)
_ax_cv.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=3))
_ax_cv.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%b %d, %Y'))
_fig_cv.autofmt_xdate(rotation=0, ha='center')

_ax_cv.set_ylim(0, 1.88)
_ax_cv.set_xlim(_train_last90.index[0] - pd.Timedelta(days=2), _cv_df['fold_index'].iloc[-1] + pd.Timedelta(days=2))

plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.06, right=0.97, top=0.90, bottom=0.12)
_fig_cv
```

> [!NOTE]
> Forecasts are recursively generated every 5 days, yielding 24 evaluation cycles across the 120-day horizon.

## 6. Beyond Point Forecasting: Uncertainty Quantification & Peak Signals

While point forecasts capture the conditional mean, operational decision-makers in emergency care require **probabilistic fan charts, distribution tails, and calibrated surge triggers**.

### Can Point Forecasts Capture Peak Dynamics?

The interactive plot below demonstrates **10,000 simulated forecast trajectories**. Use the built-in slider to inspect scenario density and compare the conditional point forecast against extreme surge realizations:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_train_pr = prob_data['train_example'][-8:]
_test_pr = prob_data['test_example']
_forecasts = prob_data['forecast_example']
_scenarios_df = prob_data['probabilistic_scenarios']

_origin_date_pr = _train_pr.index[-1]

_train_dates = [d.strftime('%Y-%m-%d') for d in _train_pr.index]

_conn_actual_y = np.array([_origin_y] + list(_test_pr['ead']), dtype=np.float32)

_scenarios_matrix = _scenarios_df.to_numpy(dtype=np.float32)

_conn_scenarios = np.hstack([_origin_col, _scenarios_matrix])

_milestones = [1, 5, 25, 100, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000]

_fig_scen = go.Figure()

# Trace 0: Train

))

))

# Vectorized scenario chunk traces
_x_template = np.append(np.array(_conn_dates_pr), [None])
_num_fixed = 3
_prev_idx = 0

for _i, _count in enumerate(_milestones):
    _chunk = _conn_scenarios[_prev_idx:_count, :]
    _m = _chunk.shape[0]

    ))
    _prev_idx = _count

_slider_steps = []
for _i, _count in enumerate(_milestones):
```

### Predictive Distribution Across Horizons ($h = 1 \dots 5$)

Ridgeline kernel density estimates (KDE) demonstrate how uncertainty widens across horizons, showing where the actual outcome landed relative to the conditional point forecast and the 95th percentile risk threshold:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_test_pr = prob_data['test_example']
_forecasts = prob_data['forecast_example']
_scenarios_df = prob_data['probabilistic_scenarios']

_palette = ['#0F4C5C', '#1B6B7A', '#20808D', '#2FA39F', '#5BBFBA']
_fig_ridge, _ax_ridge = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 7.5), facecolor='#FBFAF4')
_ax_ridge.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')

_overlap = 0.68
_x_eval = np.linspace(0.0, 2.35, 450)
_n_horizons = 5

for _i in range(_n_horizons):
    _y_base = _i * _overlap
    _vals = _scenarios_df.iloc[:, _i].to_numpy()
    _kde = gaussian_kde(_vals)
    _density = _kde(_x_eval)
    _peak = _density.max()
    _density_norm = (_density / _peak) * 0.90

    _ax_ridge.plot([0.0, 2.35], [_y_base, _y_base], color='#94a3b8', linewidth=1.4, alpha=0.6, zorder=_i*4+1)
    _ax_ridge.fill_between(_x_eval, _y_base, _y_base + _density_norm, color=_palette[_i], alpha=0.55, zorder=_i*4+2)
    _ax_ridge.plot(_x_eval, _y_base + _density_norm, color='#0B363C', linewidth=2.0, zorder=_i*4+3)

    _act_val = float(_test_pr['ead'].iloc[_i])
    _fc_val = float(_forecasts[_i])
    _q95_val = float(np.percentile(_vals, 95))

    _act_h = float(_kde(_act_val)[0] / _peak * 0.90)
    _fc_h = float(_kde(_fc_val)[0] / _peak * 0.90)
    _q95_h = float(_kde(_q95_val)[0] / _peak * 0.90)

    # Actual Observed
    _ax_ridge.plot([_act_val, _act_val], [_y_base, _y_base + _act_h], color='#C93B2B', linewidth=3.0, zorder=_i*4+4,
                   label='Actual Observed EAD' if _i == 0 else None)
    _ax_ridge.scatter([_act_val], [_y_base + _act_h], color='#C93B2B', s=70, zorder=_i*4+5, edgecolor='#ffffff', linewidth=1.2)

    # Point Forecast
    _ax_ridge.plot([_fc_val, _fc_val], [_y_base, _y_base + _fc_h], color='#2563EB', linewidth=2.6, linestyle='--', zorder=_i*4+4,
                   label='Point Forecast' if _i == 0 else None)
    _ax_ridge.scatter([_fc_val], [_y_base + _fc_h], color='#2563EB', s=75, marker='D', zorder=_i*4+5, edgecolor='#ffffff', linewidth=1.2)

    # 95th Percentile
    _ax_ridge.plot([_q95_val, _q95_val], [_y_base, _y_base + _q95_h], color='#D97706', linewidth=2.4, linestyle=':', zorder=_i*4+4,
                   label='95th Percentile' if _i == 0 else None)
    _ax_ridge.scatter([_q95_val], [_y_base + _q95_h], color='#D97706', s=70, marker='^', zorder=_i*4+5, edgecolor='#ffffff', linewidth=1.2)

    _ax_ridge.text(_act_val, _y_base + _act_h + 0.07, f'{_act_val:.2f}', color='#C93B2B', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='bottom')
    _ax_ridge.text(_fc_val, _y_base + _fc_h + 0.07, f'{_fc_val:.2f}', color='#2563EB', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='bottom')
    _ax_ridge.text(_q95_val, _y_base + _q95_h + 0.07, f'{_q95_val:.2f}', color='#D97706', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='bottom')

    _ax_ridge.text(-0.03, _y_base + 0.18, f'Horizon {_i+1}', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C', ha='right', va='center')

_ax_ridge.set_xlim(-0.02, 2.35)
_ax_ridge.set_ylim(-0.1, (_n_horizons - 1) * _overlap + 1.25)
_ax_ridge.set_xlabel('Estimated Avoidable Deaths (EAD)', fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C', labelpad=12)
_ax_ridge.set_yticks([])
_ax_ridge.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=12, colors='#334155')
_ax_ridge.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.45, color='#cbd5e1')
for _sp in ['top', 'left', 'right']:
    _ax_ridge.spines[_sp].set_visible(False)
_ax_ridge.spines['bottom'].set_color('#94a3b8')

_ax_ridge.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=True, facecolor='#ffffff', edgecolor='#cbd5e1', fontsize=13, framealpha=0.95)
plt.tight_layout()
_fig_ridge
```

### Can Calibrated Uncertainty Bounds Capture Peaks in EAD?

By constructing 80% and 90% predictive intervals, we can assess empirical coverage reliability over the 120-day holdout:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_train_last90 = cv_data['training_last90']
_cv_df = cv_data['cv_results']
_origin_date = _train_last90.index[-1]
_n_total = len(_cv_df)

_fig_pi, _ax_pi = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 7.5), facecolor='#FBFAF4')
_ax_pi.set_facecolor('#FBFAF4')

# Historical Training
_ax_pi.plot(_train_last90.index, _train_last90['ead'], color='#64748b', linewidth=2.2, label='Historical Training EAD', zorder=3)
_ax_pi.fill_between(_train_last90.index, 0, _train_last90['ead'], color='#64748b', alpha=0.06, zorder=2)
_ax_pi.axvline(_origin_date, color='#0B363C', linestyle='--', linewidth=2.4, zorder=8, label='Forecast Origin')

# Prediction Interval Bands
_ax_pi.fill_between(_cv_df['fold_index'], _cv_df['lower_90'], _cv_df['upper_90'], color='#20808D', alpha=0.15, zorder=4, label='90% Prediction Interval')
_ax_pi.fill_between(_cv_df['fold_index'], _cv_df['lower_80'], _cv_df['upper_80'], color='#20808D', alpha=0.28, zorder=5, label='80% Prediction Interval')

# Forecast & Actuals
_ax_pi.plot(_cv_df['fold_index'], _cv_df['y_pred'], color='#2563EB', linewidth=2.6, linestyle='--', marker='s', markersize=4.2, zorder=7, label='MS-ARR Point Forecast')
_conn_dates = [_origin_date] + list(_cv_df['fold_index'])
_conn_actuals = [_train_last90['ead'].iloc[-1]] + list(_cv_df['y_true'])
_ax_pi.plot(_conn_dates, _conn_actuals, color='#C93B2B', linewidth=2.8, marker='o', markersize=4.2, label='Actual Observed EAD', zorder=8)

# Empirical Coverage
_cov_80 = ((_cv_df['y_true'] >= _cv_df['lower_80']) & (_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df['upper_80'])).mean() * 100
_cov_90 = ((_cv_df['y_true'] >= _cv_df['lower_90']) & (_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df['upper_90'])).mean() * 100

_metric_text = (f'Probabilistic Calibration (120-Day Horizon):\n'
                f'• 90% Empirical Coverage: {_cov_90:.1f}%\n'
                f'• 80% Empirical Coverage: {_cov_80:.1f}%')
_ax_pi.text(0.015, 0.96, _metric_text, transform=_ax_pi.transAxes, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C',
            va='top', bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.55', facecolor='#ffffff', edgecolor='#20808D', linewidth=1.8, alpha=0.96), zorder=10)

_ax_pi.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.32, 0.96), frameon=True, facecolor='#ffffff', edgecolor='#cbd5e1', fontsize=12, ncol=2)
_ax_pi.set_ylabel('Avoidable Deaths (EAD)', fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C')
_ax_pi.set_title('80% & 90% Calibrated Prediction Intervals vs. Observed Out-of-Sample Harm', fontsize=17, fontweight='bold', color='#0B363C', pad=18)
_ax_pi.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.35, color='#cbd5e1')
_ax_pi.tick_params(labelsize=12)
_ax_pi.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=3))
_ax_pi.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%b %d, %Y'))
_fig_pi.autofmt_xdate(rotation=0, ha='center')

_ax_pi.set_ylim(0, 1.92)
_ax_pi.set_xlim(_train_last90.index[0] - pd.Timedelta(days=2), _cv_df['fold_index'].iloc[-1] + pd.Timedelta(days=2))

plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.06, right=0.97, top=0.90, bottom=0.12)
_fig_pi
```

### Operationalizing Forecasts into Actionable Peak Signals

In healthcare operations, a point forecast often under-predicts the magnitude of extreme surges. By coupling the **upper quantile ceiling** with an operational escalation threshold ($\text{th}$), clinical teams can preemptively activate surge protocols:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: false
_cv_df = cv_data['cv_results']
_n_total = len(_cv_df)
_thresholds = [0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2]
_bounds = ['90', '80']

_fig_ops = go.Figure()

# Base Traces
_fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=_cv_df['fold_index'], y=_cv_df['y_true'],
    mode='lines+markers', name='Actual Observed EAD',
    line=dict(color='#C93B2B', width=3.2),
    marker=dict(size=7.5, color='#C93B2B'),
    hovertemplate='<b>Actual EAD:</b> %{y:.2f}<br>Date: %{x|%b %d, %Y}<extra></extra>'
))

_fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=_cv_df['fold_index'], y=_cv_df['y_pred'],
    mode='lines+markers', name='Point Forecast (y_pred)',
    line=dict(color='#2563EB', width=2.6, dash='dash'),
    marker=dict(symbol='square', size=7, color='#2563EB'),
    hovertemplate='<b>Point Forecast:</b> %{y:.2f}<br>Date: %{x|%b %d, %Y}<extra></extra>'
))

_fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=_cv_df['fold_index'], y=_cv_df['upper_90'],
    mode='lines+markers', name='Upper 90% Bound',
    line=dict(color='#0B363C', width=2.6),
    marker=dict(symbol='triangle-up', size=6, color='#0B363C'),
    hovertemplate='<b>Upper 90% Bound:</b> %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>',
    visible=True
))

_fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=_cv_df['fold_index'], y=_cv_df['upper_80'],
    mode='lines+markers', name='Upper 80% Bound',
    line=dict(color='#20808D', width=2.4, dash='dot'),
    marker=dict(symbol='triangle-down', size=6, color='#20808D'),
    hovertemplate='<b>Upper 80% Bound:</b> %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>',
    visible=False
))

# Scatter Traces for Surge Classifications
_combo_traces = {}
_curr_idx = 4

for _b in _bounds:
    _col = f'upper_{_b}'
    for _th in _thresholds:
        _th_r = round(_th, 2)
        _surges = _cv_df['y_true'] > _th_r
        _normal = _cv_df['y_true'] <= _th_r
        
        _safe_mask = (_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df[_col]) & _normal
        _correct_mask = (_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df[_col]) & _surges
        _wrong_mask = (_cv_df['y_true'] > _cv_df[_col]) & _surges
        _pt_miss_mask = (_cv_df['y_pred'] <= _th_r) & _surges
        
        _fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_cv_df.loc[_safe_mask, 'fold_index'], y=_cv_df.loc[_safe_mask, 'y_true'],
            mode='markers', name='Safe Demand',
            marker=dict(color='#10B981', size=8), hovertemplate='<b>Safe Demand:</b> %{y:.2f} EAD<extra></extra>',
            visible=False
        ))
        _fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_cv_df.loc[_correct_mask, 'fold_index'], y=_cv_df.loc[_correct_mask, 'y_true'],
            mode='markers', name=f'Correct Surge (≤ Upper {_b}%)',
            marker=dict(symbol='diamond', color='#0284C7', size=9.5), hovertemplate='<b>Surge Enveloped:</b> %{y:.2f} EAD<extra></extra>',
            visible=False
        ))
        _fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_cv_df.loc[_wrong_mask, 'fold_index'], y=_cv_df.loc[_wrong_mask, 'y_true'],
            mode='markers', name=f'Overrun Breach (> Upper {_b}%)',
            marker=dict(symbol='x', color='#DC2626', size=11, line=dict(width=2.2)), hovertemplate='<b>Surge Overrun Breach:</b> %{y:.2f} EAD<extra></extra>',
            visible=False
        ))
        _fig_ops.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_cv_df.loc[_pt_miss_mask, 'fold_index'], y=_cv_df.loc[_pt_miss_mask, 'y_true'],
            mode='markers', name='Point Forecast Miss',
            marker=dict(symbol='circle-open', color='#DC2626', size=15, line=dict(width=2.4)), hovertemplate='<b>Point Missed Surge!</b><br>Actual: %{y:.2f} EAD<extra></extra>',
            visible=False
        ))
        
        _combo_traces[(_b, _th_r)] = list(range(_curr_idx, _curr_idx + 4))
        _curr_idx += 4

_total_traces = len(_fig_ops.data)

def _get_kpi_text(target_b, th):
    n_surges = int((_cv_df['y_true'] > th).sum())
    col = f'upper_{target_b}'
    corr = int(((_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df[col]) & (_cv_df['y_true'] > th)).sum())
    wrong = int(((_cv_df['y_true'] > _cv_df[col]) & (_cv_df['y_true'] > th)).sum())
    safe = int(((_cv_df['y_true'] <= _cv_df[col]) & (_cv_df['y_true'] <= th)).sum())
    pt_capt = int(((_cv_df['y_pred'] >= th) & (_cv_df['y_true'] > th)).sum())
    
    denom = corr + wrong
    containment_rate = (corr / denom * 100) if denom > 0 else 100.0
    pt_capt_pct = (pt_capt / n_surges * 100) if n_surges > 0 else 0.0
    status_color = '#10B981' if wrong == 0 else '#DC2626'
    
    return (
        f"<span style='font-size:18px;'><b>Peak Containment Rate [Correct / (Wrong + Correct)]:</b></span> "
        f"<span style='color:#2CA0AB; font-size:24px;'><b>{containment_rate:.1f}%</b></span> "
        f"<span style='font-size:16px; color:#0B363C;'><b>({corr}/{denom} surges)</b></span><br>"
        f"<span style='font-size:13.5px;'>"
        f"• Safe EAD: <b>{safe}/{_n_total} ({safe/_n_total*100:.1f}%)</b> &nbsp;|&nbsp; "
        f"• Correct Signals: <b style='color:#2CA0AB;'>{corr}/{_n_total} ({corr/_n_total*100:.1f}%)</b> &nbsp;|&nbsp; "
        f"• Wrong Signals: <b style='color:{status_color};'>{wrong}/{_n_total} ({wrong/_n_total*100:.1f}%)</b> &nbsp;|&nbsp; "
        f"• Point Forecast Capture: <b style='color:#DC2626;'>{pt_capt}/{n_surges} ({pt_capt_pct:.0f}%)</b>"
        f"</span>"
    )

def _make_slider_steps(target_b):
    steps = []
    for _th in _thresholds:
        _th_r = round(_th, 2)
        vis = [False] * _total_traces
        vis[0] = True
        vis[1] = True
        vis[2] = (target_b == '90')
        vis[3] = (target_b == '80')
        for idx in _combo_traces[(target_b, _th_r)]:
            vis[idx] = True
            
        shape = dict(type='line', xref='paper', x0=0, x1=1, y0=_th_r, y1=_th_r, line=dict(color='#DC2626', width=2.0, dash='dash'))
        ann_threshold = dict(
            xref='paper', x=0.99, y=_th_r, xanchor='right', yanchor='bottom',
            text=f' Alert Threshold: {_th_r:.1f} EAD ', showarrow=False,
            font=dict(color='#DC2626', size=14, family='Arial Black'),
            bgcolor='rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92)', bordercolor='#DC2626', borderwidth=1.2, borderpad=3
        )
        ann_kpi = dict(
            xref='paper', yref='paper', x=0.0, y=-0.22, xanchor='left', yanchor='middle',
            text=_get_kpi_text(target_b, _th_r), showarrow=False, align='left',
            font=dict(size=12, color='#0B363C'), bgcolor='#ffffff', bordercolor='#20808D', borderwidth=1.6, borderpad=8
        )
        steps.append({
            'method': 'update',
            'label': f'{_th_r:.1f} EAD',
            'args': [{'visible': vis}, {'shapes': [shape], 'annotations': [ann_threshold, ann_kpi]}]
        })
    return steps

_steps_90 = _make_slider_steps('90')
_steps_80 = _make_slider_steps('80')

_slider_90 = dict(
    active=2,
    currentvalue=dict(prefix='Alert Threshold (th): ', font=dict(size=15, color='#0B363C')),
    font=dict(size=12, color='#0B363C'),
    bgcolor='#e2e8f0', activebgcolor='#20808D', bordercolor='#20808D', borderwidth=1.5,
    pad=dict(t=15, b=5), steps=_steps_90, len=0.38, x=0.62, y=-0.14
)
_slider_80 = dict(
    active=2,
    currentvalue=dict(prefix='Alert Threshold (th): ', font=dict(size=15, color='#0B363C')),
    font=dict(size=12, color='#0B363C'),
    bgcolor='#e2e8f0', activebgcolor='#20808D', bordercolor='#20808D', borderwidth=1.5,
    pad=dict(t=15, b=5), steps=_steps_80, len=0.38, x=0.62, y=-0.14
)

# Apply initial state
for _i, _v in enumerate(_steps_90[2]['args'][0]['visible']):
    _fig_ops.data[_i].visible = _v

_updatemenus = [
    dict(
        type='buttons', direction='right', x=0.0, y=1.12, yanchor='bottom', xanchor='left',
        showactive=True, active=0, bgcolor='#ffffff', bordercolor='#20808D', borderwidth=1.6,
        font=dict(size=13, color='#0B363C'),
        buttons=[
            dict(label=' Upper 90% Bound (Ceiling) ', method='update',
                 args=[{'visible': _steps_90[2]['args'][0]['visible']},
                       {'shapes': _steps_90[2]['args'][1]['shapes'], 'annotations': _steps_90[2]['args'][1]['annotations'], 'sliders': [_slider_90]}]),
            dict(label=' Upper 80% Bound ', method='update',
                 args=[{'visible': _steps_80[2]['args'][0]['visible']},
                       {'shapes': _steps_80[2]['args'][1]['shapes'], 'annotations': _steps_80[2]['args'][1]['annotations'], 'sliders': [_slider_80]}])
        ]
    )
]

_fig_ops.update_layout(
    shapes=_steps_90[2]['args'][1]['shapes'],
    annotations=_steps_90[2]['args'][1]['annotations'],
    updatemenus=_updatemenus,
    sliders=[_slider_90],
    xaxis=dict(title='Date (Rolling 120-Day Horizon)', gridcolor='#E2E8F0', tickfont=dict(size=12, color='#0B363C')),
    yaxis=dict(title='Emergency Avoidable Deaths (EAD)', range=[0.15, 1.90], gridcolor='#E2E8F0', tickfont=dict(size=12, color='#0B363C')),
    plot_bgcolor='#FBFAF4', paper_bgcolor='#FBFAF4',
    height=680,
    margin=dict(l=50, r=40, t=90, b=130),
    legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='bottom', y=1.02, xanchor='left', x=0.0, font=dict(size=13, color='#0B363C'), bgcolor='rgba(255,255,255,0.92)')
)

_fig_ops
```
